must_equal_approved_in_cli._added: 2026-08-08 — after auth_mode landed, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN moved here from must_be_absent_in_cli.
must_equal_approved_in_cli._why: Before this, nothing set it legitimately, so 'must be absent' was right. Now, in loopback_dummy mode hb-run explicitly injects it from the hash-locked plan, so the 'absent' criterion neither holds nor is what we actually want to prove. What we want to prove: the hostile ambient value lost to the plan value.
must_equal_approved_in_cli._note: 🔴 This is a **tightening**, not a loosening: from 'it is absent' to 'it is present, and is exactly the approved public constant, and is not the hostile value'. All three must hold. A criterion written by someone else being changed by the person writing production itself needs review — already sent for external cold review.

ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.compared_by: sha256(value), evidence written by the spawned CLI itself

cli_controlled_values.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: loopback URL assembled from this attempt's READY port and capability path

inspector_port_expectation.meaning: 2026-08-08 external review ruled (b): production inspector always binds ('127.0.0.1', 0) and reads the kernel-assigned port back from READY. The oracle no longer requires an explicit test-only injection channel. HB_INSPECTOR_PORT=43137 must be absent from the spawned inspector environment; that absence plus requested==0 is the ambient-isolation evidence. A different port number is NOT evidence — the kernel could legitimately hand back 43137. fake_inspector.py still carries --test-listen-port/--test-no-bind for other fixtures, but this case must not use them: _test_only.no_bind cannot impersonate a kernel-assigned port.
